title: Preparing a show in the dressing room before the first performance
summary: McRae insisted on finished rehearsed shows from the first performance, as he did at the Zanzibar and Roxy.

"All right, come back tonight, we're have rehearsal again." Just skim down -- just run down the act.
I say, "I want yall to come back down take your (inaudible) music again." Everybody had music.
What we would do, we would add the rest of the music to it. Now we gonna run the show down like they gonna play tomorrow on stage.
A lot of shows get a lot of bands come in, they had to stop in the middle of the act or something to go wrong, get the tempos wrong and other stuff. No, not with me.
My idea -- if you're gonna do something, do it in the dressing room. This where we had rehearsed it.
Now we get on the stage, that's it.
The public don't pay to come hear you rehearse no show. A lot of bands go in the Apollo Theater, people wouldn't catch the first show.

When they say the band is together, the show was together. No, no, no. Every show I would play was together.
When I opened the Zanzibar, I had to open the Zanzibar for one --
I had one date there. I had five or six hours to put that show together. And that's the way that show stayed together, because when I doubled in the Roxy Theater, that show was together.

And then we were going back to the Apollo Theater, when that (inaudible) first day, first show that I played for Schiffman, he admitted that no band -- he heard This is the only band (inaudible) come in there.
